title: Function calling parse debug scratchpad (Ryan)
content:
Context:
- Intermittent customer report: function/tool calling responses sometimes produce unparsable JSON when using the hosted API with streaming enabled. Repro is flaky but reproducible in ~1/8 requests under load.
- Seems correlated with long arrays in the payload + temperature > 0.

Symptoms observed:
- Client side JSON.parse throws: "Unexpected token T in JSON at position 134" or "Unexpected end of JSON input".
- Raw stream capture shows valid JSON up to a point, then a stray text fragment ("Partial summary: This model thinks...") appended, then remaining JSON chunk.
- When streaming disabled, responses are usually valid.

Commands / repro attempts (timestamped):
- 2025-11-02 09:12 - curl (no streaming):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
    -d '{"input":"generate items","modalities":["text"],"temperature":0.7,"max_tokens":512,"function_call":{"name":"write_items","arguments_schema":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object"}}}}'
  -> JSON okay, returns array of objects, size 24.

- 2025-11-02 09:18 - curl with streaming (Transfer-Encoding: chunked) + small buffer:
  -> Example stream fragments captured (assembled):
     {"items":[{"id":1,"text":"foo"}, ... ,{"id":12,"text":"bar"}]}
     Partial summary: This model tends to repeat when asked to list many items
     {"items":[{"id":13,"text":"baz"}, ... ]}
  -> JSON.parse fails because of the inserted plain text between JSON objects.

- 2025-11-03 11:00 - python requests stream iteration (requests.iter_lines):
  for chunk in resp.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True):
    print(repr(chunk))
  -> saw chunk starting with "data: {\"items\":...}" then a chunk: "data: Partial summary: ..." then data: {\"items\":...}.
  -> hypothesis: model produced an explanatory assistant message inserted into the stream mid-output (system/content mixing).

Error snippets (copied):
- "Unexpected token P in JSON at position 256"
- "Unterminated string at line 1 column 478"
- Server-side logs (runtime):
  [2025-11-02T09:18:22Z] stream-chunk worker-12: wrote chunk size=2048
  [2025-11-02T09:18:23Z] model-output: <assistant content-part (type=text)>: "Partial summary: ..."
  [2025-11-02T09:18:23Z] model-output: <assistant content-part (type=json)>: {"items": ...}
  -> ordering shows text piece between structured json parts.

Hypotheses:
1) Model sometimes emits an assistant-level commentary token in between function/tool JSON outputs due to stochasticity (temperature > 0). This commentary is not function call payload but appears in the same stream.
2) Streaming assembler on our side concatenates all assistant parts without filtering by content-type or function_call wrapper. We assume function call payload always contiguous. Broken when commentary interleaves.
3) Kernel-level tokenization or chunk boundary leads to a split where content-type metadata is lost and we accidentally treat text as data.
4) Client libraries (older SDK) may be aggregating lines incorrectly (e.g., not respecting 'data: ' prefixes or event types).

Quick mitigation tried:
- Force temperature=0, disable streaming -> success rate 99.9% OK.
- Add server-side filter: drop chunks that match /^Partial summary:/ -> reduces failures but hacky and misses other phrases.
- Switch to function_call explicit interface (function_call: {name: 'write_items'}) so model should return a single function call object. Observed reduction in interleaving but not eliminated.
- Increase model max_tokens to avoid truncation mid-JSON -> minor improvement.
- Added guardrail: only accept data with a valid top-level JSON parse; if parse fails, attempt to extract first/last balanced JSON object via brace matching. This recovers ~60% of failures but is brittle.

Notes / observations:
- Failure cases often include long arrays (>= 20 items) and occasionally when model self-annotates.
- When function_call is used and the assistant returns {"name":"write_items","arguments":"{...}"} as a string (arguments as JSON string), we then double-parse and sometimes get escaped quotes causing parse failures. Two variants seen:
  a) arguments: {"items":[...]} (good)
  b) arguments: "{\"items\":[...] }" (bad) -> leads to extra quoting layer.
- Client SDKs: older Node SDK v0.7.1 had a bug where it stripped the initial chunk's event type header causing misalignment. Possibly contributing.

Repro checklist (what to run to reproduce reliably):
1) Use streaming=true, temperature=0.7, prompt: 'Return a JSON array named items with 30 small objects. Also include a one-line summary afterwards.'
2) Capture raw stream bytes (do NOT auto-join lines). Save and inspect delimiting 'data:' events.
3) Look for any 'text' type events between json pieces.

Potential fixes and implementation notes:
- Short term (server-side):
  * Enforce that if assistant emits a function_call payload, all following content parts for that assistant turn are aggregated as the function_call payload until the call is closed. Filter out stray text parts while the function_call is open.
  * When streaming, prefix function_call json chunks with explicit event metadata (e.g., data-type: function-json) so clients can filter reliably.
  * Add a streaming schema event that signals "structured-output-start" and "structured-output-end".

- Medium term (model + prompting):
  * Use stricter system prompt: "When asked to return machine-readable JSON, ONLY output the JSON and do not include commentary." Add explicit examples and negative examples.
  * Encourage function_call with arguments as JSON object (not string) via schema in the API.

- Client SDK changes:
  * Update Node SDK to parse SSE events robustly: keep event-type, discard non-data events, and implement a streaming JSON assembler that respects explicit markers.
  * Provide helper that tries safe-json-parse: first try JSON.parse, then attempt balanced-brace extraction, then fall back to returning raw string with parse_error flag.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm whether same issue exists on Dedicated/private clusters (ask infra team) -> assign to @Ashwin.
- [ ] Add telemetry around stream events: count of non-json assistant chunks when function_call in-progress. -> create INF ticket.
- [ ] Patch Node SDK (v0.7.2) with improved SSE parsing. -> PR drafted GH: repo/sdk-js#PR-210.
- [ ] Add integration test that streams large arrays and asserts no interleaved text.
- [ ] Evaluate model steering changes with eval set (prompt set: streaming-json-eval-2025).

Random notes / thoughts to self:
- Might be easier to have the runtime collapse assistant parts into a single structured payload before emitting to customers. Extra latency but safer.
- Watch out for escaping heuristics: if model returns arguments as a string, our server should attempt to detect and unescape if valid JSON string.
- Consider adding explicit Content-Length-like metadata for structured payloads in streaming.

Snippets (useful commands):
- jq sanity: cat raw_stream.txt | sed -n 's/^data: //p' | jq -s '.[0]'
- crude brace matcher (bash):
  perl -0777 -ne 'while(/(\{(?:[^{}]|(?-1))*\})/g){ print "$1\n" }' raw_stream.txt

If I get time: instrument a small service emulating client assembly logic to fuzz different chunk boundaries and validate heuristics.

End of scratchpad.
